title_en: The Danger of Trading in the Word of Truth
body_ar:
عندما يتغلغل الإيمان في القلوب لا يمكن لأي قوة بشرية أن تقف أمامه، فهاهم سحرة فرعون عندما خامر الإيمان شغاف قلوبهم لم يخشوا تهديد فرعون بالقتل والصلب وإنما قالوا: اقض ما أنت قاض إنما تقضي هذه الحياة الدنيا. فعلى العلماء والدعاة أن يسعوا إلى زيادة الإيمان وتقويته، حتى يواجهوا به ضغوطات الجبابرة والطغاة، وأن يقولوا كلمة الحق ولا يخافوا في الله لومة لائم.
ضرورة معرفة نعم الله علينا:
إن الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا ومن سيئات أعمالنا، من يهده الله فلا مضل له، ومن يضلل فلا هادي له، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وأصحابه وسلم تسليماً كثيراً: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا وَبَثَّ مِنْهُمَا رِجَالًا كَثِيرًا وَنِسَاءً وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي تَسَاءَلُونَ بِهِ وَالأَرْحَامَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيبًا [النساء:1] ، يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَقُولُوا قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا * يُصْلِحْ لَكُمْ أَعْمَالَكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَقَدْ فَازَ فَوْزًا عَظِيمًا [الأحزاب:70-71]...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* When faith penetrates deep into hearts, no human power can stand before it. Here are Pharaoh's magicians: once faith had mingled with the innermost of their hearts, they did not fear Pharaoh's threat of killing and crucifixion, but said instead, "Decree what you will decree; you decree only for this worldly life." So the scholars and those who call people to God must strive to increase faith and to strengthen it, so that by it they may meet the pressures of the tyrants and the despots, and must speak the word of truth and not fear, where God is concerned, the reproach of anyone who reproaches.

## The necessity of knowing God's blessings upon us

Praise belongs to God. We praise Him and seek His help. We take refuge with God from the evils of our own selves and from the ill of our deeds. Whomever God guides, none can lead astray; whomever He leads astray, none can guide. I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, who has no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger — God bless him, and his family and his Companions, and grant them abundant peace. {O mankind, be mindful of your Lord, who created you from a single soul and created from it its mate, and from the two of them spread abroad many men and women. And be mindful of God, in whose name you ask of one another, and of the ties of kinship. God is ever watchful over you} (Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:1). {O you who believe, be mindful of God and speak a word that is sound; He will set right your deeds for you and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys God and His Messenger has won a great triumph} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:70-71) …

The subject announced by the title, the danger of trading in the word of truth, is never reached, and neither is the subject of the section heading. The complete text sits behind /medias/doc/c-c-28.doc. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and completes nothing. Must not be rendered as a whole lesson.

flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT, style guide section 11. This is Qur'an, Sūrat Ṭā Hā 20:72, but the synopsis presents it as reported speech with no quotation marking and no reference, unlike every other scriptural citation on the page. The English reproduces it exactly as served and adds nothing; the reference is recorded here rather than restored into the text. Note also that the received text reads 'فَاقْضِ مَا أَنْتَ قَاضٍ' — the source drops the connective. The house convention of curly braces for Qur'anic quotation has deliberately not been applied, because doing so would silently correct the source.

flags.arabic: ولا يخافوا في الله لومة لائم
flags.context: the closing clause of the site's synopsis
options: and not fear, where God is concerned, the reproach of anyone who reproaches
and fear no one's blame in God's cause
and not fear any censure for God's sake
flags.note: A fixed Qur'anic phrase (Sūrat al-Māʾidah 5:54) used here as ordinary idiom rather than as a citation, and unmarked in the source as in the previous case. The literal shape has been kept because the doubled root ('لومة لائم') is part of what the phrase does.

translator_notes: One of a run of six records, IDs 701-706, in the written-da'wah section, all uploaded on 9 May 2011 within about twenty minutes of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/c-c-* series. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lesson was delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.
Qur'anic renderings here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The transcribed portion is the khuṭbat al-ḥājah, the standard opening formula of a sermon, and nothing beyond it. This is precisely the case style guide section 9 describes.

'خامر الإيمان شغاف قلوبهم' is rendered 'faith had mingled with the innermost of their hearts'. 'شغاف' is the pericardium, used idiomatically for the deepest part of the heart; 'خامر' is to mix with and suffuse.
No ruling term from the five-rulings table appears anywhere in the record.
